criteria.remark: Two images, one on each of two pages, carry no text alternative of any kind: a large hero graphic on the home page and a profile avatar on the account page. Neither has alternative text, an accessible label, or any marking that would tell assistive technology to skip it, so anyone using a screen reader hears nothing in their place and loses whatever the image conveys. These are the non-text items that could be checked automatically on the pages reached; other non-text content on the product still needs separate review.

Sixteen in-page links across five pages point to destinations that do not exist: the header skip link targets "main-content" and news links target "news", but after pressing Enter no element on the page carries that id or name, so focus does not move and the link does nothing for a keyboard user. What was measured is only that those destinations are missing. A person has to decide whether another mechanism bypasses the same blocks — a heading, a landmark or a collapsible block. skip-link-works could not look on 1 of 37 scans (the path is replayed once for each rule, and this rule needed its end loaded again); what it would have found is not shown.

Eighteen links across six pages give a screen reader nothing to announce. Each is an icon-only link — the social links repeated in the page footer are typical — whose only content is a decorative graphic explicitly hidden from assistive technology, with no label or title standing in for it. Anyone who cannot see the icon has no way to tell where these links go, in context or otherwise. These are the links checked on the pages reached; link wording elsewhere in the product has not been examined here.

Twenty-four interactive elements across six pages are missing the name assistive technology needs to announce them. Most are icon-only links whose only content is a graphic hidden from screen readers. Also included is a form field asking for a Social Security number on the application page, which has no visible label, no associated label text and no placeholder, so it is announced only as an unnamed edit box — someone filling in that form by ear would not know what is being asked of them.

Ten pieces of text across six pages fall below the 4.5:1 minimum for normal-size text. The repeated "Last updated" line, grey on white, measures 2.81:1 at roughly 14px, and a "Pending" status badge in amber on white measures 2.27:1 — about half the required contrast. Readers with low vision, or anyone viewing the screen in bright light, may be unable to make this text out, and the status badge in particular carries meaning that is not repeated elsewhere on the page. axe could not decide 1 element under this criterion (covered by another element); they are not shown.

What was measured is only that outline's contrast against the surface behind it. A person has to decide whether another visual cue identifies the focus.
